title: The sack: lost yards, the throwaway and intentional grounding (and why Alejado "ran" for −29 yards)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The backup source (football-film-room, branch "data") couldn't be read: "repository foolserrandsf/football-film-room is not configured for this session." So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. It's a new concept from Saturday: Hawai'i's QB finished with −29 rushing yards, and a grounding penalty set up the strangest play of the night.

The big idea: a sack is when a defender tackles the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage before he throws.It costs yards and a down. 2nd-and-10 becomes 3rd-and-18.A QB under pressure has three choices: take the sack, throw it away, or force a throw. The rules decide which ones are legal.

Labels A–D match the steps below. The tackle box is the area between where the two offensive tackles line up.

  1. A · The rusher wins. Here the defensive end (DE) runs around the right tackle (RT).Saturday, Texas played LSU without left tackle Trevor Goosby. His backups had allowed 8 sacks in the two games before. Arch Manning has been sacked 27 times this season.NFL example: Houston sacked Justin Herbert 8 times in Week 9. Will Anderson Jr., Jadeveon Clowney and Sheldon Rankins had 2 each.
  2. B · The sack. The ball is spotted where the QB went down, here 8 yards behind the line.The stat rule: in college, a sack counts as a QB run. That's why Micah Alejado finished Saturday with 12 runs for −29 yards (Star-Advertiser).In the NFL, sack yards come off the team's passing yards instead. The QB's rushing stays clean.
  3. C · The legal throwaway. If the QB gets outside the tackle box, he can throw the ball out of bounds.It must reach the line of scrimmage (NFL and college). Result: an incomplete pass, no lost yards.
  4. D · Intentional grounding. Inside the tackle box, the QB can't throw to an area with no receiver just to avoid the sack.Penalty: loss of down and the ball goes back to where he threw it (in the NFL, 10 yards if that's worse). If he's in his own end zone, it's a safety (Lesson 54).Saturday: Hawai'i was flagged for grounding late. Then the officials found they had miscounted the downs, and Hawai'i got an extra 4th-and-19. It failed, and NDSU won 21-13 (Star-Advertiser).

Why it matters for bets: sacks end drives. 3rd-and-18 usually becomes a punt. That's a big reason the Texas-LSU total stayed under (43 points vs. 46.5).For a college QB rushing-yards prop, sacks count against him. A running QB facing a great pass rush can finish below zero.For an NFL QB, sacks lower team passing yards, not his passing-yards prop. His prop only drops because the drive dies.

For your Film Room drill: after a sack, it's 2nd- or 3rd-and-long. Guess pass.Then look for the fix: a tight end or back staying in to block (max protect), or a quick throw to beat the rush (Lesson 49, the hot route).

Connecting the dots: Lesson 24 counted blockers vs. rushers. Lesson 39 showed how teams help a backup tackle. This lesson is what happens when that help fails.

Video: search YouTube for "intentional grounding rule explained" and "Texas vs LSU 2026 highlights."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 6: Situations)

o: A tackle of the QB behind the line before he throws
Any tackle for a loss on a run
quiz.w: A sack is the QB tackled behind the line of scrimmage before he passes. It costs yards and a down.

quiz.q: Micah Alejado finished with 12 rushes for −29 yards. Why can a college QB's rushing be negative?
o: In college, sacks count as QB runs
Penalties are added to his runs
quiz.w: College stats count a sack as a rushing attempt. In the NFL, sack yards come off team passing instead.

quiz.q: The QB rolls outside the tackle box and throws the ball out of bounds past the line. What's the call?
quiz.w: Outside the tackle box, a throwaway is legal if it reaches the line of scrimmage.

quiz.q: In your Film Room drill, the offense was just sacked. It's 3rd-and-17. What's the best guess?
quiz.w: Long yardage is a passing down. Watch for extra blockers staying in (max protect) or a quick throw.
